title: Building an ROI Model for AI Agent Projects
author: Jason D.
excerpt: Stop guessing at value. Here's the framework we use to model ROI for agent deployments before a single line of code is written.
content:
"What's the ROI?" It's the question every AI initiative faces, and most teams can't answer it with confidence. Not because AI isn't valuable, but because they never built the measurement system.

The ROI Framework

Our ROI model has three components: cost savings, capacity gains, and quality improvements.

Cost Savings

Direct cost reduction from automation:

hours_saved_per_week = manual_time_per_task * tasks_per_week * automation_rate
cost_savings = hours_saved_per_week * hourly_cost * 52

Capacity Gains

What your team can do with reclaimed time:

capacity_value = hours_saved * value_of_redirected_work

Quality Improvements

Reduction in errors, rework, and escalations:

quality_value = (current_error_rate - target_error_rate) * cost_per_error * volume

Building the Model

Start by measuring the current state for 2-4 weeks. You need actual data:

  • How many tasks per week?
  • How long does each take?
  • What's the error rate?
  • What does an error cost?
  • What's the fully loaded cost of the people doing this work?

Then model the target state conservatively:

  • Assume 70% automation rate (not 95%)
  • Assume 90% accuracy (not 99%)
  • Include the cost of the agent (compute, monitoring, maintenance)
  • Include the cost of human review for escalated cases

A conservative ROI model that's credible beats an optimistic one that nobody believes. Under-promise, over-deliver.

The Break-Even Question

The most important output isn't total ROI — it's time to break even. If the project costs $200K to build and saves $20K/month, you break even in 10 months. Leadership can evaluate that trade-off clearly.

The Bottom Line

Build the ROI model before you build the agent. It forces clarity on what you're automating, why it matters, and how you'll measure success. That clarity alone makes projects more likely to succeed.
